elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) expressly provides that M&I's consent is not required for an assignment to a Customer Affiliate, subject to compliance with Section 21.11.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) eliminates M&I consent for an assignment pursuant to a merger involving Customer; this is broad enough to cover assignment to the merger successor, subject to Section 21.11.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) eliminates M&I consent for an assignment pursuant to an acquisition of Customer, subject to Section 21.11.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) expressly eliminates M&I consent for an assignment pursuant to a sale of all or substantially all Customer assets, subject to Section 21.11.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires the other party's prior written consent, and Section 22.4(b) specifically states that M&I may assign only with Customer's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: Both the opening sentence and Section 22.4(b) state that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(b) states that M&I may assign 'in no event to a competitor of Customer.'

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from a change in control of Customer.
elements.evidence: The change-in-control provision grants no termination right and affirmatively requires M&I to continue providing Services, although the existing entity and volume limitations remain.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) permits no-consent Customer assignments pursuant to a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, which encompasses customary successor transactions, subject to Section 21.11.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative language expressly requires written notice of a Customer successor assignment. The contents of cross-referenced Section 21.11 are not provided and cannot establish the missing notice duty.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(b) requires Customer's prior written consent even for M&I merger, reorganization, asset-sale, and business-successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause requires prior written consent rather than establishing a successor-assignment right conditioned only on written notice.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The Affiliate carve-out permits Customer to assign to an Affiliate without M&I consent even where that Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: For Customer assignments requiring M&I consent, the opening sentence expressly provides that such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence and Section 22.4(b) require Customer's prior written consent for M&I assignments; no no-consent Vendor carve-out remains.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: Although the clause generally states that Customer consent may not be unreasonably withheld, it categorically prohibits assignments to Customer competitors. That exception permits no consent determination under the fallback's unqualified reasonableness standard.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Customer receives the requested Affiliate and transaction assignment carve-outs, Vendor assignments require Customer consent subject to a reasonableness standard, competitor assignments are prohibited, and no change-of-control termination right is created. The fallback is not independently satisfied because there is no mutual successor-assignment regime based on written notice, and Vendor successor assignments still require consent. The redline is not strictly minimal because Customer's transaction carve-out is framed more broadly as any assignment 'pursuant to' the listed transactions and additionally references stock or securities rather than limiting the right to assignment to the transaction successor. Drafting quality is moderate because subsection (b)'s placement of the '(i)' and '(ii)' list after the competitor prohibition is syntactically awkward and creates avoidable scope ambiguity, though the intended commercial result remains discernible and unrelated change-of-control terms remain operative.
